description: Location-based salary adjustments for remote work. Companies often use geographic cost of living multipliers.

high_cost_areas.note: Baseline - these are what most salary data reflects

low_cost_areas.note: 45% adjustment - lowest cost of living areas

fully_remote_companies.typical_adjustment: Use multipliers above, sometimes less aggressive (0.7-1.0 range)

traditional_companies_gone_remote.salary_approach: Often pay based on office location, not employee location
traditional_companies_gone_remote.note: If role is 'remote from SF office', you might get SF salary regardless of where you live

startups.salary_approach: Highly variable - some ignore location, others strictly apply multipliers
startups.equity_consideration: May offer more equity to compensate for location-adjusted cash

west_virginia_specific.reality_check: WV has one of the lowest costs of living in US
strategies_for_wv_residents: Target companies with location-agnostic pay (GitLab, Zapier, some crypto/web3 companies)
Focus on high-value skills (AI/ML, blockchain, specialized niches) where talent scarcity overrides location
Negotiate hard - emphasize value delivered, not cost of living
Consider contracting/consulting at higher hourly rates
Look for companies based in medium-cost cities (not SF/NYC) - smaller adjustment
Build strong portfolio to justify top-of-band compensation regardless of location

how_to_use_in_analysis.step_3: Apply multiplier to market salary data
how_to_use_in_analysis.step_4: Provide both numbers: 'National average' and 'Adjusted for your location'
how_to_use_in_analysis.step_5: Explain strategies to maximize salary despite location
how_to_use_in_analysis.example: Software Engineer Mid-level national average: $130k. Adjusted for West Virginia (0.55 multiplier): $72k. However, some companies (GitLab, Zapier) ignore location - target those.

low_cost_area_advantages: Lower living costs mean you can save more at same salary
Highlight this in negotiations: '$75k in WV = $136k in SF in terms of purchasing power'
Emphasize remote work benefits to company: 'You save on office space, I save on rent'
Show total comp value: salary + WFH stipend + benefits + equity
what_to_ask_during_interviews: Do you use location-based pay bands?
What location is this role's salary benchmarked against?
Is there room to negotiate above the pay band for exceptional candidates?
Do you offer equity/bonuses that could offset location adjustment?
